mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates one signed difference to another, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of the names to keep the sign. This avoids turning a directional difference into an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence says "the number of X that Y has more than Z is equal to the difference between the number of A and B" (or any equivalent phrasing).
mathgap.example: Interpreting the statement as |Y - Z| = |A - B| (absolute values) instead of (Y - Z) = (A - B).

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the stated number at that point in the narrative, before any later transfers or comparisons.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence states "X has N items" (or similar).
mathgap.example: Treating "Herbert has 90 raspberries" as a permanent value, ignoring later splits that change Herbert's count.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; after solving, discard any solution that yields a negative count for any person.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system, verify each variable is ≥ 0 and an integer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person ends up with -3 peaches, which violates the problem constraints.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more oranges than Y" as X - Y = N (i.e., X = Y + N) and "X has N fewer oranges than Y" as Y - X = N (i.e., X = Y - N). Preserve the order of names to keep the sign correct.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses "more" or "fewer" to compare two persons.
mathgap.example: Reading "Abbigail has 5 more peaches than Alphonse" as |Abbigail - Alphonse| = 5, losing the direction.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X splits all the items she owns equally among Y and Z", give each of Y and Z half of X's current count, and set X's count to zero (or to the remainder if the count is odd, but counts are integers so assume even).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence describes a split‑all operation.
mathgap.example: Assuming the splitter retains her items after splitting, leaving her count unchanged.

mathgap.title: Targeted constraint extraction for queried variable
mathgap.principle: When the goal is to find a specific person's count, first collect all equations that directly involve that person, and prioritize solving those before handling unrelated constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem asks for the count of a particular individual.
mathgap.example: Solving the entire system of equations without first isolating constraints that involve the target variable, leading to unnecessary complexity.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, updating their counts for any subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence says "X gives N items to Y".
mathgap.example: Ignoring the order of transfers and using the original counts for later comparisons, causing mismatched values.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known from a direct statement or previous substitution, replace it with its numeric value before solving the remaining equation.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When an equation of the form (A - B) = (C - D) contains a difference that has already been determined.
mathgap.example: Leaving (A - B) as a symbolic term even though A and B have been assigned concrete counts, missing the opportunity to simplify the equation.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the list of statements in the order given, using the current counts at each step; earlier equations affect later ones, especially when transfers or comparisons depend on updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any problem where statements are ordered and later statements refer to counts that may have changed.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a comparison before applying a preceding transfer, thereby using stale counts.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the magnitude of the difference and drops the sign, misreading "has more than" as an unsigned relation.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Keep the order of names when translating differences; use (X - Y) = N for "X has N more than Y" and preserve sign in equalities.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats all transfers as simultaneous, forgetting that earlier transfers change counts used in later statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process statements strictly in the given order, updating counts after each transfer before evaluating subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a direct count as a permanent final value, overlooking that later transfers can modify that person's count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct count assignments as setting the current count at that point; allow later transfers to change it.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by N times" as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase "increase by N times" is read as a simple increment instead of scaling the current count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize that "increase by N times" means multiply the current count by N.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting split‑all statements as leaving the original person with zero even when they are a recipient
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the splitter always ends with zero, ignoring cases where the splitter also receives items in the same operation.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply split‑all as giving half to each recipient and setting the splitter's count to zero unless the problem explicitly states otherwise; if the splitter is also a recipient, handle that as a separate transfer.
